wording: P87 finds that male social mobility in Scotland was already extensive in 1901 (52% mobile, 30% upwardly) and grew over the twentieth century (64% and 42% in 1974; 67% and 45% in 2001; downward mobility 22% throughout), about 1.5 percentage points per decade, driven largely by structural change (the professional and managerial class rising to 46.9% of destinations in 2001); relative mobility also increased (unidiff parameters 0 in 1901, -0.24 in 1974, -0.48 in 2001). In 1901, 57% of the salariat came from manual origins.
locator: P87 Introduction to Conclusion, Tables 1-7 (read in full; supporting information not read)
confidence: Moderate (one national study; linked 1871-1901 census records plus 1974 and 2001 surveys; men only)
counterevidence_limits: Men only; 1901 data are weighted linked records (11% of cases unclassifiable); comparisons over time use a five-class scheme. Arithmetic issues in AS0-SOC-02.
operationalization: SOC Ascendence = upward intergenerational class mobility
verification_phrases: P87|The increase in upward mobility was driven by structural change || P87|The rate of that growth was about 1.5 percentage points per decade || P87|Fully 57% of men in the salariat came from manual

wording: Most of P87's printed numbers reproduce (dissimilarity indices 0.117, 0.1615, 0.232 vs 0.12, 0.16, 0.23; 28%, 17%, 46%, 57%; mobile = up + down; 241 - 183 = 58), but two pre-registered checks were not supported: Table 5's quasi-perfect-mobility reduction is 1 - 6865/30992 = 77.8%, not the printed 78.8% (text: 79%); and Table 4's salariat sample size 7344 does not follow from Table 3 (its row percentages and sizes give 6234), although Table 4's percentages do (17.0% self-recruitment, as printed). P87 states that percentages are weighted while sample sizes are unweighted, which plausibly explains the second but not the first.
counterevidence_limits: Audits printed rounded numbers; the weighting explanation is the agent's inference, since the weights are not printed.
operationalization: SOC Ascendence = auditing a mobility study
